publisher: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives
title_or_table: Statistics of the Presidential and Congressional Election of November 5, 2024 (published March 10, 2025), House races
table_id: Clerk of the House, election statistics 2024
observation_period: General election of November 5, 2024 (Louisiana’s open primary the same day; Maine’s ranked-choice tabulation as the Clerk prints it)
geography: The 435 House districts of the 50 states
universe_or_base: Each of the 435 House races: winner, runner-up, total votes, margin and the kind of seat
unit: votes; margin in percentage points of all votes cast for the office in the district
vintage: Compiled by the Clerk from official sources, published March 10, 2025
qualification: Margin is the winner’s votes less the runner-up’s, over all votes for the office, so it reads the same in every kind of seat; blank, void, over and under votes and continuing and exhausted ballots are not votes for a candidate, and a fusion candidate’s party lines are summed. A seat with one candidate on the ballot has no margin, even where write-ins drew votes. In one-party contests both top candidates share a party, so the margin is between two candidates of one party. Alaska’s figures are the first round and Maine’s 2nd district the final round, as the Clerk prints them; Louisiana’s House races were decided in the November 5 open primary.

winner_party.description: winner’s main party line as printed

winner_group.description: Republican, Democratic (Minnesota’s DFL and North Dakota’s Democratic-NPL included) or other

winner_votes.description: winner’s votes, all party lines summed

runner_up.description: candidate with the second most votes

runner_up_party.description: runner-up’s main party line as printed

runner_up_votes.description: runner-up’s votes, all party lines summed

total_votes.description: all votes for candidates and write-ins in the district

margin_pct.description: winner less runner-up, as percentage points of total votes, computed

seat_kind.description: Republican and Democratic; one-party contest (top-two); other pairing; unopposed on the ballot; ranked-choice first or final round; Louisiana open primary

candidates.description: candidates on the ballot, write-ins left out

printed_source_line: Source: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives, Statistics of the Presidential and Congressional Election of November 5, 2024, 435 House districts. Retrieved November 12, 2026. Margins computed by Oath & Action from the official counts.
derivation: For each district, the two candidates with the most votes (write-ins and ballot categories left out), their margin over all votes for the office, and the kind of seat by the rule in the qualification.
notes: Seats won by party as printed: {'Republican': 220, 'Democratic': 215}.
